summary: A pragmatic distributed lock service built on etcd transactions, leases, and watches to achieve linearizable mutual exclusion with automatic cleanup. It correctly emphasizes fencing tokens (from committed revisions) to keep downstream state safe under partitions and long pauses, and it outlines solid operational practices for etcd-backed coordination.
strengths: Uses proven etcd primitives (transactions/leases/watches) for linearizable locking and liveness without inventing custom consensus
Explicit fencing-token story with downstream enforcement guidance, plus realistic ops/monitoring considerations
weaknesses: Contention behavior is underspecified (fairness/starvation, thundering herd on watch wakeups, and mitigation patterns like queued contenders)
Missing key production details: authn/authz/ACLs and quotas, watch compaction/revision handling edge cases, and more concrete capacity limits/benchmarks for the stated QPS/key counts
